A campus built from observation.

40 photo galleries, street-level views, architecture sources and elevation references used to guide the recreation. Photographs remain at their original sources; they are visual references, not copied game textures. Modelled façades and many dimensions remain approximations.

COLLEGES JOURNAL

Kensington Colleges · Bates Smart project journal

Printed pp. 180–183 / PDF pp. 92–93: five- and six-storey volumes step up the terrain. Courtyard faces have faceted glazed brickwork, balconies and narrow windows; outer faces use a three-shade clinker brick blend. Photographs inspected, not redistributed.

Open source ↗
COLLEGES COURTYARD

Kensington Colleges · Google Street View courtyard

Street-level courtyard: pale faceted brick bays, narrow dark window frames, recessed balconies, concrete floor edges, planted retaining edges and timber seating. Used as a visual reference only.

FIG TREE HALL

Fig Tree Hall · official UNSW exterior

COLLEGES AERIAL

Kensington Colleges · electrical contractor aerial gallery

Aerial view confirms courtyard-facing zigzags, projecting exterior balcony boxes, tan flat roofs with rows of vents, rooftop lawns and open steel pergolas. Positions and dimensions of reconstructed details remain approximate.

REPORTED HEIGHTS

NSW planning assessment · Library and Mathews heights

June 2020 B22 assessment, printed p. 22 / PDF p. 28: Library 57.74 m; Mathews 54 m. Reported overall heights supersede the conflicting 60 m OSM tags in this model; individual roof parts are not surveyed.
